label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Kavya, I’ve been thinking about your post and the conversations around it. I don’t want this to become a public fight between us, but I do want to correct a few things and own where I got it wrong.

We were both part of Foundry91 cohort 4. Before demo day in March, you sat with me in the Koramangala office until 1 am fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. You didn’t have to do that. You’ve helped me a lot, and I haven’t forgotten it.

Here’s what happened from my side.

DabbaDost posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. One person applied on 19 September, and the second came as a referral roughly two weeks later. Nobody from my side DMed either of them.

The offers were 22% over their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined us on 3 November.

You also mentioned that we promised ESOPs we don’t have. We do have an ESOP pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January.

I knew where both of them worked from day one. I should have called you before making the offers, not after the second one was accepted. That’s on me.

I did WhatsApp you after the second offer was accepted, but you didn’t respond before the post went up. I can understand why hearing it at that point might have felt too late.

I also want to leave the two people who joined us out of this. They made their own decisions and didn’t ask to be part of a public conversation.

We have 11 startups in this batch, and many of us hire from the same small pool around HSR and Koramangala. This will happen again. Maybe we can agree on a simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer. Not to ask permission, but so there are no surprises.

Kavya, I respect what you’re building at SitterNest and I value our friendship. I’m sorry I didn’t handle the conversation better. Coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re comfortable. I’d rather talk to you than have the rest of this conversation in LinkedIn comments.
